fluctuations in binding to a single site, rctA, of two proteins (RctB and ParAB2) that are essential for chromosome replication and segregation, respectively, underlies a regulatory network controlling these essential processes.

fluctuations in the binding of ParB (ParB2) to the centromere-like site (parS) in rctA underlies a regulatory network that controls both the firing of the replication initiator (RctB) and the production of ParB (the essential partitioning protein) for chromosome II (chr II) replication and segregation.
the rctAB operon and the parAB2 operons are involved in a regulatory cross-talk that controls chromosome II replication and partitioning in Vibrio cholera.
